full_judgment: 2. The relevant facts, for the disposal of this appeal, are that the writ respondent filed the aforesaid writ petition, stating that one Giasuddin got allotment of the disputed plot in 1957. He mutated his name in the khatian and different government offices. Giasuddin died in 1992 leaving his sister Lutfun Nessa as his only heir. She also mutated her name in different Government offices. Thereafter, Lutfun Nessa transferred the disputed plot to the writ petitioner respondent by a deed dated 17.01.2005. On 18.05.2005, the writ petitioner filed an application in the office of Housing and Public Works Departments for getting her name mutated and it was allowed. On 23.11.2006, the writ respondent-appellants cancelled the order of mutation. Thus, the writ petitioner instituted the aforesaid writ petition and obtained Rule Nisi.
